summary: Implement tag-driven Slack onboarding gateway + project bootstrap automation
description: Issue summary: Request to deliver a tag-driven onboarding gateway that provisions Slack channels, creates a matching Jira project bootstrap, and links a Confluence space using a single claim flow. Impact: currently team leads create channels and projects manually which leads to inconsistent metadata, missing owners, and unclear archival schedules. This prevents automation (retention, billing attribution) and increases support burden. Request: build an automated gateway (bot + Jira workflow + Confluence template) that accepts a small set of tags (team:, sensitivity:, lifecycle:) and performs: 1) create Slack channel with metadata and default channel settings; 2) create Jira project using 'team' tag and attach standard issue templates; 3) provision a Confluence space from the 'project bootstrap' template and add channel link; 4) register ownership and automated archival TTL based on lifecycle tag. The gateway should support claim-by-owner, request approval for private channels, and generate a traceable audit entry in the admin log. Security notes: private channel creation must require approver from security for sensitivity:high. Acceptance criteria listed below.
request_details: Minimal UX: slash command /create-project-boot or a self-service form in the provisioning portal. Tags accepted: team:<identifier>, sensitivity:{low|medium|high}, lifecycle:{ephemeral|standard|longterm}, purpose:<short text>. Default rules: ephemeral -> 30d archival TTL, standard -> 180d, longterm -> no auto-archive. Channels created under prefix team-<identifier>. Jira project key auto-suggest, Confluence space key aligned. Audit entry must include requestor and approver and link to created artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Slash command or portal triggers channel+Jira+Confluence creation in a single flow. 2) Created Slack channel contains pinned message with metadata tags and owner claim instructions. 3) Jira project created with template 'Project-Bootstrap-V2' and initial issue set (onboarding checklist). 4) Confluence space created and linked back in Slack channel and Jira project. 5) Audit log entry written to admin-runbook and visible in ops-dashboard. 6) Sensitivity:high requires manual approval before private channel is created. 7) TTL enforcement runs and archives ephemeral channels after 30 days if unclaimed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Attempt manual creation today: results are inconsistent. 2) Submit an example request via the existing manual onboarding doc and record missing fields. 3) Observe support tickets created for missing owners and retention misconfiguration. This ticket is to replace that manual workflow with an automated gateway.
investigation_notes: - Spike conducted by platform-infra on 2026-03-05 validated Slack API scoping for channel metadata and discovery. - Confluence template requires minor adjustments to inherit project key. - Existing Jira provisioning lambda can create projects but lacks tag-driven inputs. - Approval flow best implemented via GitHub-style SSO+approver webhook or simple Slack modal with approver list. Hypothesis: combination of Slack bot + infra lambda + Jira API + Confluence REST will be sufficient. Potential blockers: mailbox for approvers, rate limits on Confluence creation during onboarding events.
risks_and_mitigation: Risks: accidental creation of private channels without approval, mis-specified lifecycle leading to premature archival, privilege escalation via bot scopes. Mitigations: require approver for sensitivity:high, preview modal with TTL warning, limited bot scopes and audit logs, implement permission checks in Jira project creation lambda.
work_items: Extend provisioning lambda to accept tags
Add approval webhook and approver list config
Wire Confluence template to bootstrap flow
timeline_proposal: Week 1: design and security review; Week 2: implement bot + lambda extension; Week 3: integrate Jira & Confluence creation; Week 4: QA in staging and runbook; Week 5: gradual rollout behind feature flag.
